OCD Live

A proposal prepared for Bovann Group: an end-to-end booking system for 90-minute live-selling sessions on the House of Challenge TikTok account, in the Lomé studio or remotely from 17 countries, extended by a business toolkit, a supervised agent, an academy and a 318-page book.

Key engineering decisions

01

Small payload for slow networks

The audience is on mobile data in West Africa, so no framework and on-demand loading of the book text.

02

Payment rails as data

Each country maps to its operators, so adding a market is configuration rather than code.

Notes for reviewers

Limits and next stepsA real deployment needs a server database, authentication for the four roles and the payment provider outside Cameroon still to be chosen.
01

Problem statement

Bovann, who leads the OCD movement on TikTok, opened the House of Challenge account to members who want to sell. Arranging those sessions by message does not scale: the team needs to know who is coming, what is sold and when, and an isolated seller needs visibility (product, telephone number and address on screen) before any sale can take place. The brief, given in two recorded video requests, called for a system covering the whole cycle from the choice of slot to payment and notification.

02

Contribution

A six-step booking flow (studio or remote session, day, time, package, business details with explicit consent to display the number and address, mobile-money payment) issues a QR-coded ticket and notifies Bovann Group. The team console provides a dashboard, the studio schedule and on-screen banner, a host view that brings remote sellers on air at their local time, registers of sellers and payments, and editable prices. A live directory lets sellers list their own sessions, subject to approval in fixed review windows, and lets buyers browse by country and category in a vertical feed. After the session, each seller keeps a public page with QR code and payment links, invoices and quotes in FCFA, expense capture from receipt photographs, an agent with twelve skills and a 60-lesson academy.

03

Architecture

Static HTML, CSS and JavaScript without a framework, chosen to keep the payload small on slow mobile connections; Canvas and jsPDF render graphics and PDF documents in the browser. In the demonstration each account’s data is held in browser storage. The agent calls the Claude API when it is available and falls back to prepared responses; it prepares actions but executes none without the user’s approval.

04

Method and data

The two video briefs were transcribed locally and serve as the requirements record. The book was written from them, typeset from Markdown into an A5 PDF with headless Chrome, and its text is loaded only on request. Payment rails are modelled per country: KPay for Cameroon, and operators such as Flooz, T-Money, Wave, Airtel Money or MonCash elsewhere. The map of Africa and nineteen textile patterns, among them kente, bogolan and ndop, are drawn procedurally.

05

Verification and limitations

This is a demonstration: the data are fictitious, no real payment is processed, and the provider for countries outside Cameroon has not been chosen. The team space opens with the client’s own credentials, and the agent never sends a message or a document without explicit approval.
